judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines 'Related Party Loans' by an open-ended example ('such as a loan under which the borrower is owned by one or more of the members... or their family members'), leaving the class's outer boundary uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c064 and c058 carve specific transactions out of the Related Party Loan definition, and c073 restates the standards differently; the definition's reach is contested across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at any time shall not exceed 20% of total Company assets at such time' is a continuous test, clearly worded on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c073 states the same limit as applying only 'upon the closing of the Related Party Loan in question' — a continuous covenant versus a point-in-time test, a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'consistent with the lending standards and policies set forth above' incorporates by reference a body of standards that are themselves hedged with 'generally' and 'expects'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c073 restates the same requirement as 'must not be on terms more favorable to the borrower than similar loans negotiated at arm's-length' — a different formulation of the same covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any material event of default has occurred and is continuing for ninety (90) consecutive days' turns on 'material event of default', a term nowhere defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c073 states the trigger simply as 'if the Loan is in default more than 90 days' with no materiality qualifier and without the 'at par' price — a conflicting statement of the same buy-back obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'after consideration of all relevant factors' gives an unbounded allocation discretion, and the defined term 'Other Sponsored Investment Funds' is used interchangeably with 'Other Sponsored Funds'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c075 and c076 use 'Sponsored Investment Funds' as though defined, and c109 refers to 'a Sponsored Investment Fund'; the inconsistent labels for the same class run through the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'only so much time to the business of the Company as is reasonably required' is a vague performance standard, though a familiar fund formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c110 restates it as 'such of its business time... as may be necessary to perform its obligations', a similar but not identical standard; no genuine contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short factual disclosure about counsel; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c118's statement that Company Counsel does not represent investors.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The pricing floor is 'not less than any of the following: (i)... (ii)... or (iii)' — 'not less than any of' plus 'or' is genuinely ambiguous between the highest of the three and merely one of them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its final sentence excludes affiliate seller financing from 'Related Party Loan' status, which cuts against the c051/c052 20% limitation; c079 also permits such affiliate sales.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains an evident drafting slip — 'or later into co-investment agreements' (apparently 'enter') — and refers to 'Sponsored Investment Funds or Private Clients' without defining either.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c055 defines the class as 'Other Sponsored Investment Funds' and c075 uses 'Sponsored Investment Funds, Private Clients'; the criteria are said to be 'established by the Note Purchase Agreement', a document not before the reader.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'primarily in the United States', 'occasional loans' and 'a strict set of guidelines' are vague, and the guidelines that follow are themselves hedged with 'generally'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c063 permits up to 20% non-U.S. lending and c064 disapplies the loan-to-value ratios entirely for purchase-money financing, so 'strict' guidelines are qualified elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-row table giving 70% for improved property and 50% for land; the categories are clear but the table states no basis of valuation on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c064 supplies the valuation basis and immediately softens the table with 'generally will not exceed' and an outright exemption for purchase-money financing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Most Company loans are expected to be secured by a first deed of trust' is aspirational, but the 20% junior-lien cap is a definite limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c063, c073 and c077 each impose a separate 20% limit measured against differently described denominators ('Loan Portfolio', 'total Company Capital', 'total Company assets', 'capital of the Company'), which makes the family of caps hard to apply together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'total Company Capital' is capitalised as if defined but is defined nowhere; the document elsewhere uses 'Investor Capital', 'total Company assets' and 'capital of the Company'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c086 defines 'Investor Capital' and c052/c073 use 'total Company assets'; the undefined denominator here cannot be reconciled with those measures without construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'generally will not exceed the percentages stated above' converts a stated cap into a soft target, 'based a valuation' drops a word, and the Manager may itself supply the valuation instead of an appraisal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies c061's ratios for purchase-money financing and declares such financing not to be a 'Related Party Loan', which narrows c051/c052's affiliate protections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will vary at the discretion of the Manager' and 'generally have a term of between one (1) and six (6) years' impose no binding limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A six-year loan made near the final closing in 2009 would mature after the Notes' December 31, 2014 Maturity Date in c089 and near the outer limit of the Company term in c106 — a maturity mismatch across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clearly subordinates credit evaluation to the loan-to-value test and openly permits lending to defaulted borrowers; blunt but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leans entirely on 'the loan-to-value ratios described above', which c064 makes non-binding ('generally') and disapplies in stated cases.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory escrow instruction; 'until the following conditions are met' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item (c) in the list that follows (c070) is not a condition at all but a disclaimer, which undermines this framing sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Satisfactory title insurance coverage' leaves the standard of satisfaction unstated, though the amount is fixed to the loan principal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with c067 and c071; no contrary provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Satisfactory fire and casualty insurance' is again an unstated standard, and 'or only casualty insurance in the event of a Loan secured by unimproved land' is oddly phrased.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c151 warns that certain risks may be uninsurable or insurable only below replacement cost, which sits uneasily with a mandatory escrow condition; the cross-reference to 'Uninsured Losses' points to a Risk Factor heading that does not exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item (c) is drafted as a disclaimer of intent, not a condition to disbursement, so it does not fit the list it belongs to.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c067 introduces (a)-(d) as 'conditions' that must be 'met' before funds are disbursed; (c) cannot be met or unmet, an incoherence within the enumerated list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Company investments in Loans will not be held in the name of the Manager or any other nominee' is an absolute and clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c060 permits investing 'indirectly in a loan by acquiring an ownership interest in an entity formed for the sole purpose of holding a qualifying loan', which is in tension with the no-nominee rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes servicing and payment mechanics; 'anticipated' softens it but nothing needs construing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'either directly to the Company or to the Servicer for deposit in the Servicer's trust account' leaves the custody route optional, which interacts with c093's segregated-account regime but does not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'must be purchased from the Company by the Manager or its affiliate rf the Loan is in default more than 90 days' contains an OCR-level error and, more importantly, compresses three separate covenants into one run-on sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts c052 (continuous 20% test versus this closing-date test) and c054 (which requires a 'material event of default' and purchase 'at par'); the two statements of the same restrictions cannot both be operative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Generally, the purchase price... will not exceed the par value of the note or its fair market value, whichever is lower, but the Manager may purchase loans from unaffiliated parties for a premium' — the exception plus 'generally' largely swallows the rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c075 requires affiliate-related purchases to be 'priced at fair market value or better for the Company', a different pricing standard from this one; c058 supplies yet a third pricing formula for defaulted-loan sales.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or to achieve comparable with Sponsored Investment Funds' is missing a word, and 'a purchase from, sale to, of a co-investment with' contains a further error; the criteria are also deferred entirely to an unseen agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires acquired loans to be 'fully performing', which conflicts with c079's permission to sell non-performing Portfolio Loans to affiliates and with c059's expectation of purchasing loans from R.E. Loans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long double-negative permission ('None of the Company... is precluded from') with a proviso; parsable but clumsy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers the affiliated-transaction criteria to the Note Purchase Agreement, whereas c051-c054 and c075 state such criteria in the Memorandum itself — overlapping and not identical sources of the same restriction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'After the second year of the Company's term' is ambiguous about when the term began (initial closing? formation?), and 'the capital of the Company' is another undefined denominator.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c106 measures the Company's term from an unstated start to a Maturity-Date-plus-two-years end, giving no clear anchor for 'the second year', and c063/c052 use different capital measures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Wholly permissive ('may be retained', 'if the Manager believes'), with an open-ended list of permitted holdings ending in 'or other liquid assets'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Funding the reserve 'from any source, including capital raised from the sale of Notes' fits c019 but sits against c012's promise that Note capital funds Portfolio Loans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not presently intend' and 'may occasionally sell' state no obligation, and 'for the purposes of restructuring... or re-positioning the property for sale' is a broad justification for affiliate sales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits sales of non-performing loans to affiliates, which conflicts with c020's 'will not source loans for the purpose of resale' and with c075's 'fully performing loan' requirement for affiliate transactions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Explanatory rather than operative; the borrowing permission itself is stated in one clear sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c108 is the operative Company Borrowing provision and permits senior liens on the Collateral; this section's cross-reference to 'Risks and Other Important Factors - Risks of Leverage' points to a heading that does not exist in Section VII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Investors whose Note Purchase Agreements are accepted in the discretion of the Managing Member' uses 'Managing Member', a term never defined anywhere in the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c084/c088 vest that acceptance discretion in the 'Manager' and c027/c084 define 'Managing Directors'; 'Managing Member' also reappears in c185, so the mismatch is systemic rather than a one-off typo.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the Company as a Delaware LLC; a naming line with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c013 and c048's reliance on Delaware law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'such other directly related activities... as the Manager deems reasonably necessary or appropriate' is a general catch-all following specific enumerations, the classic ejusdem generis setting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c013 states the purpose in different terms ('commercial real estate or for other real estate related purposes') and c113 protects 'the general purpose of the Company' from amendment without defining it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company may admit additional or substitute managers' is stated without any condition or Noteholder protection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c109 forbids the Manager to 'withdraw as the sole manager' without a Majority in Interest, which is hard to square with an unconditional right to substitute managers; c168 also says Noteholders have no power over admissions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines 'Servicer' collectively for 'one or more qualified servicing entities' while naming a single initial Servicer; 'qualified' is unspecified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c031 says the Servicer 'will not take a direct role in the Company's management' while this delegates sourcing, origination and administration to it; c050 adds that other firms may act 'in lieu of' the Servicer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Investor Capital, Portfolio Loans, Portfolio Borrowers and the Program; the definitions are OCR-mangled but plain, and 'no minimum or maximum' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c015's statement that no minimum or maximum has been targeted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A minimum investment is 20,000 Units, in the discretion of the Manager' is self-cancelling — a minimum that the Manager may disregard, and it is unclear whether the discretion is to waive or to raise it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c090 and c091 make subscriptions subject to Manager acceptance generally, which is consistent; nothing else fixes a minimum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ties eligibility to 'accredited investors' under the 1933 Act and to Manager acceptance; both are determinate references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c172-c182 spell out the accredited-investor criteria, and c175's 'IRREVOCABLE TRUST' formulation is narrower than Rule 501 — a mild mismatch with this general reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Maturity Date is defined twice — once as the December 31, 2014 date subject to a six-month extension and again as 'the last day of the Note's term' — and 'The Floating Rate will not be less than 8% on an annualized basis for a calendar year' is unclear as between a per-quarter floor and an annual average.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c016 states the same rate term as a 'minimum average rate of eight percent (8%) annualized' rather than a floor, and c124 uses 8% only as a tax Comparable Yield expressly disclaimed as any representation of amounts payable — a real conflict about the core payment obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward payment mechanics defining 'Principal' by reference to the purchase price paid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c089's Roll-over Interest and c091/c092's additional-Unit purchases both increase Principal by book entry rather than reissue, which is consistent with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'no additional subscriptions... will be accepted by the Manager for any closing after the final closing' is definite; 'qualified investor' is used where the document elsewhere says 'accredited investor'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c172 requires suitability standards to be met at the time of any increase, which matches; c099 fixes the final closing date, so the two work together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Manager may request or permit... voluntary purchase of additional Units' followed by 'In order to accept an offer to sell additional Units by the Company' conflates a request by the Manager with an offer by the Company.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps substantially with c091 and repeats the same no-reissue sentence; the two paths to additional Units are not clearly distinguished.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two segregated accounts are described in parallel and clearly; 'unaffiliated institutional lender' as the custodian is an odd choice of words but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Company may retain interest earned on investor deposits, which sits against c018's characterisation of Noteholders as creditors but is expressly agreed here; no operative conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'unless either of such conditions is waived by the Company' plus 'entirely within the discretion of the Company to grant or deny' makes the prepayment right wholly illusory — one-sided drafting a court could construe against the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c017 describes the same right as available after 'a minimum of one year' without mentioning the 60-day notice or quarter-end requirement, and c096 accelerates everything on bankruptcy; the summary and this text are not aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actions of the Collateral Agent shall be binding on the Noteholders' combined with agent powers 'on terms required by the Manager' is broad, though limited by 'only to the extent that such terms or actions are not prohibited under the Noteholder Agreements'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 50% threshold is measured by 'Principal and accrued Interest' whereas c109 defines 'Majority in Interest' by 'aggregate outstanding principal' alone — two different majorities in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'except to the extent the Company's obligations... have been assumed by an affiliate of or successor in interest to the Company' is an unusually broad exception to acceleration, with no consent requirement or creditworthiness standard for the assuming affiliate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits an affiliate substitution that c109's Majority-in-Interest consent rights (merger, consolidation, dissolution) would otherwise appear to control, and it is precisely the clause that would be litigated in the Company's bankruptcy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'with the requisite approval of members' leaves the required approval unspecified in a company whose sole member is the Manager itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c048 notes the Manager is the sole member, so a member-approval condition is circular; c049 and c168 acknowledge future members may be Manager affiliates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a minimum capital investment of $25,000' is a definite figure and the Note-purchase permission is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c015 says affiliates may purchase Notes 'on the same terms', matching this; c095 excludes affiliate-held Notes from consent calculations, which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the last day of the end of the sixth full quarter after the Initial Closing' is redundantly phrased and ambiguous about whether a partial quarter counts, which is why the parenthetical estimate is needed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c015 states closings run 'through May 1, 2009' from an initial closing 'on or before December 3, 2007', while this fixes December 1, 2007 and an estimated June 30, 2009 — a direct date conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise fee formula payable monthly in advance on prior-month-end balances.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c038; c109 bars direct salaries in any month a Portfolio Management Fee is payable, using a fee label that appears nowhere else as a defined term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'not to exceed a maximum of $500,000 or 1% of aggregate Principal of outstanding Notes, whichever amount is greater' is a cap that grows with the offering and is unclear as to the measurement date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c045 states the same Company Expenses definition with no cap at all; one of the two must yield, and the reimbursement obligation to the Manager turns on which governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Servicer will be entitled to retain the following additional compensation paid by third parties' is followed by a sweep of any such fees paid to the Company itself to the Servicer, which is broader than 'paid by third parties'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives Loan Process and Documentation Fees as '$1,000-$2,000' where c043 says 'approximately $1,000', and states the servicing fee as '0.0833%' monthly where c039 says '1/12 of 1%'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence allocating Loan Service Expenses to the Servicer; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c046 and complementary to c044/c101.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An open list of fees ('or other fees') payable to affiliates by Portfolio Borrowers, expressly 'subject to restrictions with respect to Affiliated Transactions' — a capitalised term defined nowhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision in the Memorandum defines 'Affiliated Transactions'; c051-c054, c075 and c076 each state affiliate restrictions in different terms, so the qualifier has no fixed referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'restrictions in the amount of compensation it may receive' says the Company is restricted in compensation it receives, when the restrictions described elsewhere concern compensation the Company pays — an apparent drafting slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Sections III and IV for 'summaries of these restrictions', but c051-c054 and c073 state those restrictions inconsistently with each other.
